history.new: The common-border formula (H-C01-7) holds for all 2159 relations tested, including 1326 hard relations not covered by Theorem 5.

hypothesis: H-C01-7: with k = |u| = |v|, q = alphabet size and c(x) = 1 + sum over words b that are borders of both u and v of x^(k-|b|), the class counts are the coefficients of c(x) / (x^k + (1 - q x) c(x)) (= the number of length-n words avoiding any single word whose autocorrelation is c).
methodology: Exact class counts by union-find. 'Hard' pairs are those where neither border set contains the other (the case not covered by the proved containment theorem); for k <= 5 binary and k <= 3 ternary all pairs are tested.
question: Is the number of classes of length-n words modulo u <-> v determined by the common borders of u and v?
